chunks: And with this chain, from this chain from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Mufaddhal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Any believer who withholds a believer's wealth while he is in need of it, by Allah, he will not taste the food of Paradise nor will he drink from the sealed drink.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual punishment for withholding a believer's wealth?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the severity of withholding wealth from a needy believer by linking it to the denial of specific celestial delights: the food of Paradise and the 'sealed nectar' (al-rahiq al-makhutum) mentioned in Surah Al-Mutaffifin. This hadith underscores the spiritual weight of financial rights (huquq al-nas) in Shia ethics, where depriving a brother in faith is not merely a social slight but a barrier to experiencing divine bounty in the afterlife. The warning serves as a potent reminder that material hoarding during one's life directly impacts one's spiritual sustenance in Jannah.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. Sinan from al-Muffadhal from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who withholds the wealth of a believer which he needed, by Allah, he will never taste the food of Paradise nor will he be able to taste the sealed drink of Paradise.”
